scope: Targeted technical investigation after a frozen identity- and label-hidden visual-QC flag; no clinical interpretation or label use
interpretation: The nearly blank ADC patch reproduces zero-valued native ADC pixels around the supplied point. It is not caused by out-of-bounds sampling, padding, clipping, or a resampling failure. Geometric containment and common frame identifiers therefore do not establish usable ADC signal support at this finding.
protocol_constraint: The frozen protocol states that exact native or interpolated zero values alone are not an exclusion criterion and that visual impressions cannot alter series selection without a separately approved qualified-review protocol before outcome analysis.
decision: Because no qualified image reviewer is available, retain the finding and patient in their frozen fold under the original zero-value policy. Disclose the native ADC support limitation and require sensitivity analyses that omit this finding from ADC-only and paired-channel evaluations. Do not remove it from T2-only evaluation, replace the patient, or move the finding between folds.
resolution_basis: This conservative retain-and-report decision avoids a post hoc exclusion based on one AI-flagged image while still measuring whether the finding materially affects ADC-only or paired-channel results.
next_step: Proceed with frozen model-development inputs and prespecify primary-versus-sensitivity reporting for ADC-only and paired-channel analyses.
